change.problem: The new in-memory first-output validation rejects Torch's TorchVersion string subclass because environment metadata requires an exact built-in str. Earlier JSON round-tripping normalized the value before validation.
change.fix: Normalize torch.__version__ with str(...) in the shared environment producer; preserve strict receipt validation.

selection.scope: Three explicitly selected authored native-serving functions; failure-call parameterization yields four cases per invocation. No broad suite or scientific execution.

attempts.observation: The success fixture and supervisor-template fixture failed at first-output in-memory validation; the later-failure case encountered ValueError before its intended encoder RuntimeError. The first-call encoder-failure case passed.

attempts.source_inputs: The corrected runner and test identities in change.checked_source_inputs.
attempts.observation: A distinct corrected invocation passed all expected cases and reached the actual baseline CLI child. Both invocation results and their original captures are retained.

controlled_supervisor_fixture.scope: Controlled supervisor assignments are not real child processes. The excluded count covers unsuccessful assignment slots, including absent or malformed observations. Native in-process code prepares the template; the single real CLI child is accounted for separately.

checked_engineering_obligations: The complete ordered first batch undergoes real in-memory validation while its cumulative first-output span is still null and the call is running.

The clock observer returns actual perf_counter values and confirms sampling after successful validation. Finite, nonnegative first-output spans remain unchanged through later snapshots and the final receipt.
The cumulative span encloses measured load plus the first raw call. The actual CLI child's parent process duration encloses its cumulative span.
Failure before first output leaves the span null; failure on the subsequent warmup call preserves the first-output observation.
Missing, null and non-enclosing first-output spans are rejected. An accepted successful receipt paired with exit code 7 is excluded from successful-assignment samples.
Job and run schema revisions are /2; package, policy and batch revisions remain /1.

methods.inventory_changes_between_attempts: Only the corrected runner and test source pins changed. The other reviewed source inputs and runtime inventory remained equal.
methods.startup: Normal existing venv startup, including reviewed hooks in the parent and actual CLI child.
methods.authoritative_outcome: Retained result.json plus JUnit case identities and outcomes; the PowerShell launcher does not propagate pytest failure as its shell status.

trust_and_scope_limits: These are authored local engineering fixtures, including native CPU inference and one actual baseline CLI child after correction. They do not establish production behavior or a serving performance advantage.
Observers add overhead. Counts and timestamps identify execution attempts and outcomes; no measured latency is published as a performance result, resource saving or business impact.
The reviewed source/runtime inventories are partial content inventories, not a complete Python/native dependency attestation or operating-system sandbox. Existing bytecode reads remain possible.
Recorded installation metadata does not establish historical lockfile agreement.
Capture commitments bind retained private bytes; they do not independently attest execution, freshness, privacy, Git ancestry or the complete runtime.
Absolute local paths, raw logs, environment values and native timing observations are omitted from this public derivative.
No scientific study, training, archived evaluation, historical replay or live provider request was performed.
Hosted CI and review outcomes are separate post-commit evidence. The configured engineering selection does not revalidate the opt-in raw-text-serving module.
Issue #14 c1/c5 remain partial/open; controlled OS cold-cache behavior, memory/energy savings and ROI remain unsupported.
